script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Morning, Sarah. August 5th already. Feels like another day on The Daily Tanu-chan Show.
script.ja: おはようございます、サラさん。もう8月5日ですね。『たぬちゃん毎日ショー』の別の日って感じです。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Good morning, Alex. You look like you need that coffee.
script.ja: おはよう、アレックス。そのコーヒーが必要な顔してるね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, definitely. (sips coffee) It's drizzling out there, did you notice? Feels a bit heavy.
script.ja: ええ、本当に。 (コーヒーを飲む) 外は小雨が降ってますよ。ちょっと重たい感じがします。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I did. My tea tastes better when it's like this, somehow. Looks like a high of 31 today, even with the rain.
script.ja: ええ、そうね。こんな日は紅茶が somehow 美味しいのよ。雨でも最高気温は31度みたいね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, really? Even with the drizzle. I was hoping it would cool down. My office is always so hot in summer.
script.ja: ああ、そうなんですね？小雨でも。涼しくなるかなと思ったのに。うちのオフィスは夏はいつもすごく暑いんですよ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I know the feeling.
script.ja: その気持ち、わかるわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Anyway, did you see the news about Kabuki? This new 'Roppongi Kabuki' thing. It sounds really accessible.
script.ja: そういえば、歌舞伎のニュース見ました？この新しい『六本木歌舞伎』ってやつ。すごく身近に感じられそうですね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yes, I saw that. They called it the 'most accessible Kabuki ever.' Shorter performances, easier to understand stories.
script.ja: ええ、見たわ。『史上最も親しみやすい歌舞伎』って言ってたわね。上演時間が短くて、物語もわかりやすいって。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, 'the advent of a new Kabuki style.' What does 'advent' mean, actually?
script.ja: そう、『新しい歌舞伎スタイルの到来（advent）』って。その『advent』ってどういう意味なんですか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It just means the start or arrival of something important. A new era, you could say.
script.ja: それはね、何か重要なことの始まりとか到来を意味するの。新しい時代、って言ってもいいわね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Ah, I see. A new era for Kabuki then. I've only been once, and honestly, I didn't really get it. Four hours is a long time. My little one would never sit through that.
script.ja: ああ、なるほど。じゃあ歌舞伎の新しい時代ですね。僕、一度しか行ったことないんですけど、正直、あんまりわからなかったんです。4時間は長いですよね。うちの子は絶対座ってられませんよ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: No, probably not. Even my kids find it a bit much. This new format might bring in younger audiences, which is good.
script.ja: ええ、無理でしょうね。うちの子たちもちょっと長いって思うわ。この新しい形式は若い観客を呼び込むかもしれないわね、それは良いことだわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: True. And then there was that ukiyoe painting news. Rediscovered, right? With the courtesans in the cold.
script.ja: 確かに。それから、浮世絵のニュースもありましたね。再発見された絵画。寒そうな遊女たちが描かれたやつ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It sounds beautiful. Fukagawa in winter, preparing for something. I love those old woodblock prints. It's always nice when something like that gets found again.
script.ja: 素敵ね。冬の深川、何かを準備している女性たち。ああいう古い木版画、私も好きだわ。ああいうものがまた見つかるのは、いつも嬉しいことね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Definitely. Oh, and the immigration news. Tougher rules for permanent residency? Income and pension. I feel like I read this headline every year.
script.ja: 本当に。ああ、それと入管のニュース。永住権の取得条件が厳しくなるんですか？所得とか年金。毎年この見出しを読む気がします。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: They're proposing to require applicants to maintain income above the average for Japanese households. And certain pension contributions.
script.ja: 申請者に、日本の世帯平均所得以上の収入と、特定の年金拠出を維持することを求める提案だそうよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Right. So, if your income isn't high enough, that would kind of... preclude you, wouldn't it? Preclude? Is that the right word?
script.ja: なるほど。じゃあ、収入が十分じゃないと、それがちょっと… preclude（プレクルード）するってことですか？プレクルード、で合ってます？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yes, it means it would prevent you from getting it. It would make it impossible to meet the requirements.
script.ja: ええ、そうよ。それはあなたがそれを手に入れるのを妨げる、という意味ね。要件を満たすことができなくなる、と。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, I guess it would. It's a big hurdle, especially for young families. You know, trying to save up and maintain a certain income level with a baby, it's not easy.
script.ja: ええ、そうでしょうね。特に若い家族にとっては大きなハードルです。ほら、貯金しようとして、赤ちゃんがいる中で一定の収入レベルを維持するのって、簡単じゃないですから。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It certainly does. It’s always a balance.
script.ja: 本当にそうね。いつもバランスが大事だわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: And speaking of today, tomorrow is August 6th, right? Hiroshima Peace Memorial Day.
script.ja: そういえば、今日のことなんですが、明日って8月6日ですよね？広島平和記念日。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yes, that's tomorrow. It's when the peace memorial ceremony is held in Hiroshima. A very important day for Japan, for remembering.
script.ja: ええ、明日よ。広島で平和記念式典が開催される日ね。日本にとって、そして追悼にとって、とても大切な日だわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, I didn't know the exact date, but I always think about it around this time of year. It's a heavy thought for a morning.
script.ja: ええ、正確な日付は知らなかったんですけど、毎年この時期になるといつも考えます。朝からちょっと重い話ですね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It is. But remembering is important. On a lighter note, my cucumbers are doing really well in the garden this year. I've been making a lot of sunomono.
script.ja: そうね。でも思い出すことは大切だわ。もう少し軽い話題だけど、今年は庭のキュウリがすごくよく育っているの。酢の物をたくさん作ってるわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, really? That's nice. I keep meaning to try gardening, but with the baby and work, I don't know where I'd find the time.
script.ja: ああ、そうなんですね？それはいいですね。僕もずっとガーデニングをやってみたいと思ってるんですけど、赤ちゃんもいるし仕事もあるし、どこで時間を見つければいいのか分からなくて。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It's a slow process. Not something you rush. You find the time when you need it.
script.ja: それは時間をかけるものよ。急ぐものじゃない。必要な時に、きっと時間を見つけられるわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I guess so. Well, I'd better get ready for my first meeting. This coffee isn't going to last forever.
script.ja: そうですね。さて、最初の会議の準備しないと。このコーヒーも永遠にはもたないし。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Have a good one, Alex.
script.ja: 良い一日を、アレックス。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: You too, Sarah. And thanks for the vocab lessons!
script.ja: サラさんも。それと、語彙のレッスン、ありがとうございました！

wikipedia.title: 広島平和記念日
wikipedia.description: 1945（昭和20）年、米軍のB29爆撃機エノラ・ゲイ号が、広島市上空で原子爆弾「リトルボーイ」を投下。毎年この日に、広島市では原爆慰霊碑の前で平和記念式典が行われる。
